explain.say: Open a book in Arabic and you start at what looks like the back! Arabic is read from right to left. Look at the board: kitab, ki, tab, means book. In Arabic script your eyes begin on the right side of the page.

faq.q: Why is Arabic written from right to left?
faq.a: Arabic grew from older Semitic scripts, Aramaic and Phoenician, that were already written right to left. Why those began that way is not known for sure; one idea is that it suited carving on stone.

faq.q: Why do Arabic letters change shape?
faq.a: Arabic letters join together, so most have different forms at the start, middle and end of a word and when standing alone. It is like joined handwriting with fixed rules.

faq.q: Which languages are written right to left?
faq.a: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu are written right to left, along with a few others like Pashto and Yiddish.
An abjad is a script that mostly writes consonants and leaves out short vowels. Arabic and Hebrew are abjads, though vowel marks can be added for learners.

faq.q: How are numbers written in Arabic?
faq.a: Numbers in Arabic text are written left to right, with the biggest place first, even though the words go right to left. Our 0 to 9 digits came to Europe through Arabic writers, from India.

facts: The digits 0 to 9 used worldwide began in India and reached Europe through the Arabic-speaking world, so they are called Hindu-Arabic numerals.
